title: Applied ML: Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Model Onboarding, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Raman
body:
Summary

This playbook describes the integrated Applied ML evaluation lifecycle at Redwood: onboarding a model into the eval harness, curating and maintaining prompt sets and benchmarks, producing quality guardrails, generating quantization profiles, and a standardized regression triage process. The goal is repeatable, observable evaluation with clear ownership, SLOs, and automated checks to prevent production regressions.

Scope and audience

- Audience: ML engineers, applied scientists, platform engineers, and SREs responsible for model serving and rollout.
- Scope: workflows and templates for onboarding models into our eval harness, creating canonical prompt sets and benchmarks, producing quantization compatibility profiles, and the regression triage escalation path.

Key principles

1. Reproducibility: evaluations must be runnable by CI and locally with the same inputs and seed.
2. Ownership: every model and benchmark has a named owner and a review cycle.
3. Observability: results must emit metrics, artifacts, diffs, and a human-readable triage report.
4. Guardrails-first: prioritize quality checks that block harmful regressions (safety, factuality, hallucination rate, latency).

High-level workflow

1. Model candidate arrives (pull request or model registry entry).
2. Owner creates/updates: model card, prompt-set, benchmark config, quantization profile job.
3. CI triggers eval-harness run: functional tests, benchmark suite, safety checks, and quantization simulation.
4. Results posted to dashboard; failing guardrails open regression triage if thresholds are breached.
5. If triage fails, model rollout is paused and a remediation plan is created.

Roles and ownership

- Model Owner: primary contact for the model (creates model card and tests).
- Eval Owner: maintains the eval harness and CI pipelines.
- Quality Lead: owns guardrail thresholds and final release sign-off.
- Quantization SME: validates profiles and signs off quantized variants.
- SRE/Platform: monitors performance SLOs and deployability.

Onboarding checklist (step-by-step)

1. Create model card (models/registry): required fields: architecture, tokenizer, training-data-clauses, license, weights-location, expected sequence-length distribution, and owner.
2. Add baseline tests to eval-harness/tests/<model>: unit tests for tokenizer, shape checks, KV cache sanity, and simple prompt generation.
3. Curate prompt set(s): create at least three representative prompt classes (short prompt, multi-turn chat, and long-context completion) with 50-200 examples each. Store under prompt-sets/<model>/ with metadata.
4. Define benchmark config: reference dataset(s), metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/EM for retrieval tasks, F1/ExactMatch for QA, embedding cosine recall@k for vector tasks).
5. Add quality guardrail assertions: e.g., hallucination_rate <= 2.5%, toxicity_score <= 0.4, latency_p50 <= 120ms on target infra.
6. Kick off quantization profiling job (see Quantization Profiles section).

Prompt set and benchmark guidelines

- Prompt set composition:
  - Minimum 150 prompts per model across classes, or 500 for customer-facing LLMs.
  - Include edge cases: truncated tokens, ambiguous instructions, and adversarial-like queries.
  - Label each prompt with intent, expected output pattern, and evaluation metric.

- Benchmarking best practices:
  - Use deterministic seeds for generation.
  - Record full generation traces (logprobs, token timelines, attention masks) for reproducibility.
  - Run at multiple temperature settings (0.0, 0.2, 0.7) and aggregate metrics.

- Example prompt metadata (CSV columns):
  - id, intent, prompt_text, gold_reference, expected_metric, difficulty_tag

Quality guardrails and thresholds (examples)

We maintain a set of automated assertions that can fail CI or flag a triage:

| Guardrail | Evaluation | Blocking if | Owner |
|-----------|------------|-------------|-------|
| Hallucination rate | Fact-checking eval vs. knowledge-base | > 2.5% absolute regression vs baseline | Quality Lead |
| Safety / Toxicity | Safety classifier score (avg) | > 0.4 | Quality Lead |
| Latency | p50 on target infra (GPU type) | > 120 ms | SRE |
| Token-efficiency | tokens_generated / useful_tokens | > 2x baseline | Product/Cost |
| Embedding drift | cosine distance vs baseline | > 0.05 | Applied ML

Guardrails are configurable per-customer for Private/Dedicated tiers; defaults described above are used for hosted candidate evaluation.

Quantization profiles and compatibility checks

Purpose: generate a quantization compatibility profile that indicates expected accuracy delta, recommended quantization recipe (bits per weight, per-channel vs per-tensor, group size), and any kernel limitations.

Profile generation steps:
1. Baseline: run eval harness on fp16 or bf16 reference weights and record metrics.
2. PTQ/SQ/QLoRA simulation: run candidate quantization recipes (4-bit, 8-bit, and mixed) on a reduced prompt-set (1000 examples) capturing accuracy metrics and worst-case examples.
3. Kernel/Runtime check: verify target runtime kernels are available (e.g., triton-optimized kernels, fused attention support).
4. Performance projection: estimate latency and memory footprint improvements using measured per-layer quantized sizes.
5. Produce profile artifact: JSON with fields: recipe_id, expected_metric_delta, failing_examples_ids, recommended_runtime_tags, confidence_score.

Quick example CLI (run inside eval-harness container):

```
# run full benchmark (deterministic)
./run_eval.sh --model-id redwood/llama-3-small --prompt-set prompt-sets/redwood/llama-3-small --seed 42 --temps "0.0,0.2,0.7" --out artifacts/llama3-small/2027-02-28

# run quantization profile (simulated PTQ)
./run_quant_profile.sh --model-path weights/llama3-small-fp16.pt --recipes recipes/4bit-default.json --sample 1000 --out artifacts/quant_profiles/llama3-small-4bit.json
```

CI integration and gating

- Every merge to model-registry triggers the eval-harness CI job.
- Jobs publish artifacts to S3: metrics.json, diffs.html, failing_examples.json, quant_profile.json, and a triage_summary.md.
- Guardrail failures create a ticket in the Regression Triage board and send an alert to #applied-ml and the model owner.

Regression triage playbook (when a guardrail fails)

1. Initial detection: CI posts failing artifacts and short summary.
2. Triage owner assigned (usually the model owner or eval owner).
3. Immediate checks (run within 2 hours):
   a. Re-run CI with --retry and fresh infra to rule out flakiness.
   b. Check model-card diffs: weight version, tokenizer changes, config changes.
   c. Inspect failing_examples.json and metrics.diffs to determine if regression is general or isolated.
4. Root-cause hypothesis (within 24 hours):
   - New training data shift? (check training-data-clauses)
   - Tokenizer change? (vocab/merge changes)
   - Quantization artifact? (profile failing_examples_ids)
   - Eval harness bug? (seed, tokenization mismatch)
5. Remediation options:
   - Revert to last-known-good model for rollout and block deployment.
   - Patch tokenizer/decoding pipeline and re-run.
   - Adjust quantization recipe or disable quantized variant until fixed.
   - Expand prompt set to reduce brittleness and re-evaluate.
6. Postmortem: all regressions that caused a rollback must produce a short incident review (owner, timeline, root cause, fix, and mitigation) within 5 business days.

Outputs and observability

- Required artifacts for every eval run (CI must publish):
  - metrics.json (flat key-values, include baseline comparisons)
  - diffs.html (human-readable visual diffs)
  - failing_examples.json (ids and exact seeds)
  - quant_profile.json (if applicable)
  - triage_summary.md (owner, quick findings, next steps)
- Dashboard: per-model timeline showing metric trends, guardrail status, and quant_profile releases.

Operational SLOs for the eval pipeline

- CI completion time: 95th percentile <= 4 hours for full benchmark suite.
- Artifact availability: artifacts uploaded and indexed within 15 minutes of CI job completion.
- Triage SLA: initial hypothesis within 24 hours; remediation plan within 72 hours.

Templates and example artifacts

- model-card-template.md: fields and examples (owner, datasets, biases, limitations).
- prompt-set-template.csv: id,intent,prompt_text,gold_reference,expected_metric,difficulty_tag.
- quant-profile-schema.json: recipe_id,expected_metric_delta,failing_examples_ids,recommended_runtime_tags,confidence_score.

Related pages and references

- Eval harness standards: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025
- Quantization best practices: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026
- Regression triage playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/applied-ml-regression-triage-playbook-2026

Appendix: common troubleshooting checklist

- Tokenization mismatch: confirm tokenizer.hash == registry.tokenizer_hash.
- Non-deterministic results: fix seed and confirm deterministic flags (generate --deterministic).
- Infrastructure noise: re-run on pinned GPU type (e.g., a100-80gb) and compare latencies.
- False-positive safety flags: review classifier thresholds and sample failing prompts.

Contact and escalation

- For eval-harness CI issues: @eval-owner (Diego Martinez)
- For quantization questions: @quant-sme (Liu Wei)
- For production regressions impacting customers: escalate to SRE on-call and Product Quality Lead.

This playbook will be reviewed quarterly or on major platform changes (runtime, tokenizer, or kernel updates). For questions or to propose edits, open a PR against this page and request reviewers listed above.
